summary: A message view and message lists ask the recipient's seat's host how far its mail got, as delivery status does, when that host keeps the seat's receipts, and say so in a new optional status_from field (db break-up step 4b, the views)

replay.detail: Nothing is written: a view only reads, and a host's answer is kept a few seconds in memory.

rules.detail: For mail whose recipient's seat runs on another host that advertises message_offsets and seat-freshness reads, GET /v1/messages/read, /v1/messages, /v1/messages/page, /v1/messages/by-key and the client's message list and detail ask that host, waiting at most a second; a host that missed is not asked by views for 30 s. The message's status is the further of this member's records and the host's answer. A list of open mail, and the client's current messages, leave out mail the host says is closed, so a page can be shorter than its limit, or empty with a cursor, and its cursor goes on as before; in the client's history the message is closed. A seat's own delivery poll and its mailbox still read only its own host.

compatibility.detail: Message views and client message resources gain an optional status_from {host, state, reason?}: answered, or unknown when the host did not answer in time, in which case status is only this member's records. It is absent wherever this member's records are the whole answer: mail to a seat on this member, to a person, or to a seat whose host does not advertise message_offsets (v0.3.25 and earlier). Clients that do not know the field ignore it and read status as before; the TypeScript, Rust and Swift clients and client-v0.schema.json model it, and conversations ls prints unknown. No member advertises a new feature.

recovery.detail: Rolling back removes status_from and the asks; views read this member's own records, as before.
